title: California security deposit cap under AB 12
requirement: Most landlords may demand at most one month's rent as security for furnished or unfurnished units; qualifying small landlords may demand up to two months' rent.
key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords
coverage_conditions: Residential rental units in California; last month's rent counts toward the deposit, first month's rent does not.
citation: Assembly Bill 12
quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

applicability.other: two months allowed only for owners of two or fewer rental properties with no more than four residential units total, held by natural persons, family trusts or natural-person LLCs

sources.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units
sources.key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months' rent for qualifying small landlords

title: California photographs before deposit deductions
requirement: From April 1, 2025 the landlord must photograph the unit after regaining possession but before repairs or cleaning, and give the photos and a written cost explanation with the itemized statement.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California where the landlord intends to deduct for repairs or cleaning from the security deposit.
citation: California state law, photographs after regaining possession
quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

sources.quoted_span: Starting April 1, 2025, landlords must take photographs of a unit after regaining possession, but before any repairs or cleaning for which the landlord intends to make a deduction from the security deposit.

title: California move-in photographs of the unit
requirement: For tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, the landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of the tenancy to document its condition.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California beginning on or after July 1, 2025.
citation: California state law, photographs at start of tenancy
quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

sources.quoted_span: For tenancies that begin on or after July 1, 2025, a landlord must photograph the unit immediately before or at the start of a new tenancy to document the condition of the unit.

title: California security deposit return and itemization
requirement: Within 21 days of the tenant leaving the unit vacant the landlord must return the remaining deposit with an itemized statement, copies of documents showing charges, and proof that repairs were completed.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in California; applies to any portion of a security deposit that remains after permitted deductions.
exemptions: A landlord may deduct only amounts reasonably necessary for rent default, tenant-caused damage beyond wear and tear, cleaning, and lease-allowed replacement of personal property or furniture.
citation: California state law, security deposit return and itemization
quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

sources.quoted_span:
All or any remaining portion of a security deposit must be returned
within 21 days
after the tenant/s leave the unit vacant.

title: California tenant screening fee cap, 2026
requirement: A landlord may charge a prospective tenant a screening fee only up to the statewide cap, must supply the credit report, a receipt and any unused portion, and may not charge it when no unit is available.
coverage_conditions: Prospective tenants screened for residential rental units in California; reusable screening reports must be accepted.
exemptions: No screening fee may be charged when no rental unit is actually available, or to applicants not considered under a first-qualified-applicant policy.
citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6
quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96
penalty: Refund of any unused portion of the screening fee to any applicant not selected.

sources.quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96

title: Berkeley 2026 Annual General Adjustment
requirement: Eligible landlords may raise 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than January 1, 2026, under the conditions and notice rules in Regulation 1148.
coverage_conditions: Fully covered Berkeley rental units whose landlords qualify under Rent Board Regulation 1148 and give the required notice.
exemptions: Does not adjust rents of tenants whose tenancy began on or after January 1, 2025 and whose rent was set under the Costa-Hawkins Rental Housing Act.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.76.110A
quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

sources.quoted_span:
adopted the Annual General Adjustment (AGA) Order for Year 2026 which will allow 
eligible landlords to increase the 2025 permanent rent ceilings by 1.0% no earlier than 
January 1, 2026.

title: Measure BB 5% cap on Annual General Adjustments
requirement: The Rent Board may not approve an Annual General Adjustment above 5% in a year, even where the Rent Ordinance CPI formula would produce a larger increase.
coverage_conditions: Landlords of fully covered rental units in Berkeley, whose yearly increase is the AGA set by the elected Rent Board.
exemptions: The cap does not stop a landlord from using banked, unused AGAs from earlier years to raise rent up to the rent ceiling.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: Annual General Adjustment cap
quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

sources.quoted_span: The maximum AGA is 5%. This means that, if the formula in the Rent Ordinance results in an AGA that is greater than 5%, the AGA approved by the Board for that year can be no more than 5%.

title: Measure BB coverage of shared-facility and government-subsidized units
requirement: Units sharing a kitchen or bath with the landlord are exempt only if the landlord lived on the property at the tenancy start; government-owned or subsidized units must be registered as fully or partially covered.
coverage_conditions: Berkeley rental units: shared kitchen or bath units, and government-owned or subsidized units including Section 8, Shelter Plus Care, VASH, LIHTC and similar subsidies.
exemptions: Partially covered: new construction with a certificate of occupancy after 1980, most single-family homes and condominiums, and certain HUD-insured or federally exempt subsidized units.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: coverage of shared-facility and subsidized units
quoted_span: Where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord, the unit will be exempt from the Rent Ordinance only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy.

sources.quoted_span: Where the tenant shares a kitchen or bath facilities with the landlord, the unit will be exempt from the Rent Ordinance only if the landlord lived in a unit on the same property at the start of the tenancy.

title: Berkeley rent control coverage by unit type
requirement: Fully covered units are subject to rent control; partially covered units and exempt units are not, with coverage turning on unit type, tenancy start date and subsidy.
coverage_conditions: Berkeley rental units: fully covered means most pre-1980 multifamily units, pre-1996 single-family tenancies and rooming houses; partially covered means post-June-1980 new construction, later single-family tenancies and most condominiums.
exemptions: Exempt: golden duplexes, units where the owner shared a kitchen or bath and lived on the property when the tenancy started, post-November 7, 2018 owner-occupied ADU tenancies, dormitories and nonprofit cooperatives.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, coverage table: rent control
quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

sources.quoted_span: Most units in multifamily properties built before 1980** Fully Covered Yes Yes Yes Yes

title: Measure BB eviction notice content and Rent Board filing
requirement: Termination notices must tell tenants that Rent Board advice is available with its phone and website, and the landlord must file notices and eviction lawsuits with the Rent Board within three business days of service.
coverage_conditions: Landlords serving notices to terminate, notices to quit, or summons and complaint in Berkeley tenancies covered by the Rent Ordinance.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: eviction notice and filing requirements
quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

sources.quoted_span: The landlord must file with the Rent Board a copy of any notice to terminate a tenancy, notice to quit, and summons and complaint no later than three business days after the tenant was served with the document.

title: Measure BB bar on eviction for refusing a new lease
requirement: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease when a fixed-term lease expires.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: just cause, failure to sign new lease
quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

sources.quoted_span: A landlord cannot evict a tenant for failing to sign a substantially similar lease upon expiration of a fixed-term lease.

title: Measure BB limits on lease-breach evictions
requirement: To evict for a lease breach the landlord must show the conduct was unreasonable and caused substantial actual damage, and the notice to stop must describe the term, violation and harm in detail.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance; material lease terms mean mutually agreed terms.
exemptions: Lease breaches that cause the landlord no actual harm cannot support an eviction.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: just cause, lease breach
quoted_span:
The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.
The landlord’s notice to the tenant to stop the violation (which is required before the landlord can serve an eviction notice) must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.

sources.quoted_span:
The alleged violation must cause substantial, actual damage to the landlord.
The landlord must demonstrate that the tenant’s behavior was unreasonable.
The landlord’s notice to the tenant to stop the violation (which is required before the landlord can serve an eviction notice) must specify the lease term, and describe the violation and resulting harm in enough detail for a reasonable person to understand.

title: Measure BB nonpayment eviction threshold
requirement: A landlord may not evict for nonpayment of rent unless the tenant owes rental debt at least equal to one month of Fair Market Rent for an equivalent unit.
coverage_conditions: Tenants in Berkeley units fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, Measure BB: just cause, nonpayment of rent
quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

sources.quoted_span: For a landlord to evict a tenant for nonpayment of rent, the tenant must owe an amount of rental debt equal to or greater than one month of the Fair Market Rent (FMR) value for a unit of equivalent size in the metro area Oakland-Fremont, CA HUD Metro FMR as determined by the US Department of Housing and Urban Development for the fiscal year in which the rent is demanded.

title: Berkeley just cause coverage by unit type
requirement: Tenants in fully and partially covered Berkeley units cannot be evicted without just cause; exempt units have no just cause protection.
coverage_conditions: Berkeley rental units that are fully or partially covered, including post-June-1980 new construction units that are exempt from rent control.
exemptions: Golden duplexes, shared kitchen or bath units, owner-occupied ADU tenancies, dormitories and nonprofit cooperatives are exempt and carry no just cause protection.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, coverage table: just cause
quoted_span:
New construction: units that were built and received a Certificate of 
Occupancy after June 1980** 
Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

title: 2026 Berkeley relocation assistance payment amounts
requirement: For owner move-in and Ellis Act evictions the owner must pay relocation assistance of $19,413, plus $6,471 more for qualifying households, starting January 1, 2026.
coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted for an owner move-in under the Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance, or removed from the rental market under the Ellis Implementation Ordinance.
citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Good Cause for Eviction Ordinance; Ellis Implementation Ordinance
quoted_span:
At its October 16, 2025 Special Meeting, the Rent Board approved relocation assistance payment increases that will go into effect on January 1, 2026.
The standard relocation assistance payment will increase to
$19,413
.
The additional relocation assistance payment for qualifying households will increase to
$6,471

title: Berkeley security deposit interest by unit type
requirement: Landlords of covered units must pay interest on security deposits; exempt units carry no deposit interest requirement.
coverage_conditions: Berkeley rental units that are fully or partially covered under the Rent Ordinance.
exemptions: Exempt unit types, including golden duplexes, shared kitchen or bath units, owner-occupied ADU tenancies, dormitories and nonprofit cooperatives, have no interest duty.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, coverage table: security deposit interest
quoted_span: Most condominiums** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

sources.quoted_span: Most condominiums** Partially Covered Yes No Yes Yes

title: Berkeley security deposit interest
requirement: Landlords must pay tenants interest on the security deposit at the end of each year, plus a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before year end.
coverage_conditions: Tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance.
interaction: Local interest duty adds to the state deposit cap.
citation: Berkeley Rent Ordinance, security deposit interest
quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

sources.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.

title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rights notice
requirement: An owner who charges a fee to process a rental application must give the applicant a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap before receiving the fee.
coverage_conditions: Owners and their agents renting residential property in Berkeley who charge an application or credit report fee.
interaction: Berkeley notice duty layers on top of the state fee cap in Civil Code 1950.6.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010
quoted_span:
the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under
California Civil Code Section 1950.6(b)

sources.quoted_span:
the owner must provide, either in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before receiving the fee, a clear and conspicuous tenant screening fee rights statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap permitted under

title: Berkeley ban on non-refundable renewal fees
requirement: An owner may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees tied to a roommate leaving or to adding or replacing a roommate.
coverage_conditions: Owners of residential rental property in Berkeley and their agents, as to existing tenants; applies despite contrary lease language.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.016
quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

applicability.other: applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary lease terms

penalty: Any lease provision violating the chapter is unenforceable.

sources.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

title: Berkeley Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, and must give written notice and a chance to respond before acting.
coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley, as to current and prospective tenants and their immediate family members.
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing and Section 8 limited exemptions; owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties; units under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units being sublet or adding or replacing roommates.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.106
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation, civil damages, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.

sources.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents
requirement: No person may sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords, and no landlord may use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units.
coverage_conditions: Residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley; binds both landlords and vendors that sell or license such algorithms.
exemptions: Excludes aggregated anonymous rental reports, products setting rent or income limits under government affordable housing guidelines, and market research, appraisals, or software research, testing or training.
citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.63
quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

applicability.other: residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley

penalty: Civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, plus damages, injunctive relief, restitution of illegal profits and attorney's fees.

sources.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.
